newsitem.title: USA: Pilot board gives its president strike discretion.
newsitem.headline: Pilot board gives its president strike discretion.

text.p: The board of the Allied Pilots Association on Friday gave its president James Sovich the authority to call a strike if talks failed with American Airlines, a board member said.

The union board's 15-3 vote, coming only a few hours before the midnight Friday (0500 GMT Saturday) strike deadline it had set, was expected but reinforced the impression that the two sides were making little progress.
Board member Marv Bryant first relayed the result to reporters.

Later, union spokesman Wally Pitts said: "The APA board of directors in open session by a vote of 15-3 voted to authorize union president Sovich to call a strike at 0001 hours February 15." He added: "At this point the strike is more likely than not."

Fort Worth, Texas-based American carries about 20 percent of the nation's air travelers. If the airline shuts down it is expected to strand thousands of passengers and could cost the economy up to $200 million a day.

The union has scheduled an 1100 p.m. (0400 GMT Saturday) satellite broadcast to its members that could further indicate whether a strike will take place. President Clinton could intervene by declaring a national emergency. That would keep planes flying for up to 60 days while a presidential emergency board tried to resolve the dispute.
